notes: Section 8 defines the author's terminology for a Lefschetz correspondence ring, a Lefschetz element, and the associated co.Lefschetzien element. The NB discusses the reversal of degrees and passage to the opposite ring; the margin proposes a ‘principe de dualité’. The lower paragraph discusses nonredundancy of 2n and a chain of numbered nonvanishing statements, with π_(2n) moved into the margin. The crop shows right-pointing arrows in parentheses; these are retained regardless of possible stronger relations. The author's following sentence repeats L^n≠0 and begins a discussion of a converse over a commutative coefficient ring. No converse was proved in this transcription work. Pencil folio 17 is at the foot; no handwritten page 15 was found on this face. Faint reversed type shows through the sheet. The nearly horizontal exponent on Λ remains marked; the neighboring L^n supports n as a candidate but the stroke alone remains ambiguous. H's editorial sections and synopses are excluded as instructed.
